paper.title: What MuseScore users ask for: unmet needs around arranging and parts

declarations.competing_interests: Ivan Svetunkov is the founder of Syntonic Labs, which develops music-arranging software.

definitions.definition: Issues in the public GitHub repository musescore/MuseScore labelled 'feature request', downloaded with the GitHub API; pull requests excluded.
MuseScore feature requests with odd issue numbers; used to explore themes and form hypotheses.
MuseScore feature requests with even issue numbers; not read during exploration; reserved for planned tests.
Fixed case-insensitive keyword rules (regular expressions in themes.py, artefact A6) applied to an issue's title and body; an issue may belong to several themes.
Feature requests matched by the theme classifier's arranging_instrumentation rule (arranging, orchestration, reduction, implode/explode, instrument change, ensemble, instrumentation, playable range).

Feature requests matched by the theme classifier's notation_engraving rule (slurs, ties, accidentals, stems, beams, tuplets, clefs, signatures, lyrics, chord symbols, articulations, dynamics, engraving).
Issues matched by a theme rule divided by all issues in the set.

evidence.description: Count of MuseScore feature requests matched by the arranging and instrumentation keyword rule, on the 654 even-numbered issues labelled 'feature request' in musescore/MuseScore (held-out set), downloaded through the GitHub search API on 2026-11-05 (lab runs RN2, RN3 and RN6; plan PL3).

Total GitHub reactions on MuseScore feature requests in each of nine keyword-defined themes, on the 654 even-numbered issues labelled 'feature request' in musescore/MuseScore (held-out set), downloaded through the GitHub search API on 2026-11-05 (lab runs RN2, RN3 and RN7; plan PL2). The computation repeats that of E1 under a second plan: the lab record version used allowed one decision rule per plan, and H1 and H2 needed different rules.

tables.description: Total GitHub reactions on the 654 held-out MuseScore feature requests (even issue numbers), by keyword-defined theme; a request can belong to several themes

limitations.statement: Themes are assigned by keyword rules on issue titles and bodies; some matches are incidental words, and issues about a theme that use other words are missed.

GitHub feature requests come from people who file issues on GitHub, mostly experienced users and contributors; they do not represent all MuseScore users. A study of Moodle found that developers write most issue-tracker feature requests while users write most forum requests (KC and Hosseini 2026, arXiv:2606.20876).
Reactions are sparse: the median exploration-set issue has none, so theme totals are driven by a few issues.

artefacts.description: Every result of the lab record (117 results of 6 runs) at full precision: the lab result's ID, its run, the quantity as the run's script named it, its conditions and its value (both as JSON). The evidence's tables give the values to four significant digits.

artefacts.description: Lab record of the study: questions, hypotheses, plans, runs, results and decisions, as an append-only, hash-chained event log (Claimset lab record specification v0.15, begun 2026-11-05; exported with claimset 0.41.2).
Python script fetch_issues.py: downloads the feature requests through the GitHub search API, one creation year per query (run RN2).
Python script split_parity.py: splits the downloaded feature requests by issue number, odd numbers for exploration and even numbers held out (run RN3).
Python script explore_top.py: lists the exploration set by reactions (run RN4).
Python script themes.py: theme classifier: fixed keyword rules and per-theme counts (runs RN5, RN6, RN7).

availability.comment: Public on GitHub. The issue texts belong to their authors and are not redistributed in this package; fetch_issues.py downloads them again. The lab record keeps the hashes of the files the runs read.

artefacts.description: The 1,289 issues labelled "feature request" in the GitHub repository musescore/MuseScore, as downloaded through the GitHub search API on 2026-11-05 (run RN2): titles, the first 2,000 characters of bodies, creation dates, states, reactions, comments and labels.
